Solar System Live: credits and licences

This file goes with index.html. The README in the project folder has the same
lists with more about how each picture was made.

PLANET AND MOON MAPS (dist/maps/)
Every map was made from pictures taken by space probes. They were joined,
cleaned, resized and, in some cases, tinted or filled in where no probe took a
picture. NASA and USGS maps are public domain; NASA is thanked as their source,
and no NASA endorsement is meant or implied.

  Earth (land and sea floor)    NASA Earth Observatory, Blue Marble Next
                                Generation with topography and bathymetry (public domain)
  Earth's water mask            Natural Earth land and lake outlines (public domain)
  Mars, Mercury, Pluto, Charon, USGS Astrogeology Science Center, from NASA
  Io, Europa, Ganymede,         mission pictures (public domain)
  Callisto, Titan, Triton,
  Phobos, Rhea, Iapetus
  Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel,      NASA 3D Resources, from Voyager 2 pictures (public domain)
  Titania, Oberon
  Deimos                        Celestia project, from Philip Stooke's maps in NASA's
                                Planetary Data System (CC0)
  Moon, Venus, Jupiter, Saturn  Solar System Scope, based on NASA imagery
  and its rings, Uranus,        (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
  Neptune, Earth's city lights  Changed here: resized, joined at the edges, recoloured a
  and clouds                    little and packed into other files.
  (Venus and Uranus are mostly drawn by Solar System Scope, not photographed.)

Textures by Solar System Scope, https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/

PLANETS ROUND OTHER STARS (src/exoplanet-data.js)
Open Exoplanet Catalogue, https://github.com/OpenExoplanetCatalogue/open_exoplanet_catalogue
Copyright (C) 2012 Hanno Rein. MIT licence (text below). It gathers results from
NASA's Exoplanet Archive, exoplanet.eu and the published papers.

CODE
  three.js                      MIT licence, Copyright (c) 2010-2025 three.js authors
                                (notice kept at the end of solar.js and wallpaper.js)
  astronomy-engine              MIT licence, Copyright (c) Don Cross
                                (notice kept at the end of solar.js and wallpaper.js)
  Simplex noise (GLSL)          MIT licence, Copyright (C) 2011 Ashima Arts, by Ian McEwan
                                and Stefan Gustavson, https://github.com/stegu/webgl-noise
  "Hash without Sine"           MIT licence, Copyright (c) 2014 David Hoskins (the hash
                                functions used for the sky scenes)
  Blackbody colour curve        A fit by Tanner Helland, published as a formula
  Coastline outlines            Natural Earth (public domain) via world-atlas
